## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 73, known as *Mohana* ("Deception"), concerns a monk who feigns ignorance during the recitation of the monastic code, deceptively claiming that he did not know a rule was included in the Pātimokkha; committing this offense requires confession and expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. The word commentary (*padabhājaniya* or "Old Commentary") preserved within the Vibhaṅga explains technical legal phrases such as *anāropite* and *āropite*, describing whether a formal charge has or has not been brought against the monk [Horner 1966]. Sukumar Dutt observes that the text's injunction—that "the offence arising therefrom is to be dealt with according to the proper form" (*yañca tattha āpattiṁ āpanno tañca yathādhammo kāretabbo*)—presupposes formal legal procedures not explicitly detailed in the Pātimokkha itself, appearing to contemplate an act of censure (*tajjaniya-kamma*) for foolishness or dissimulation [Dutt 1924].

The rule corresponds to rule 73 of the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and is treated in the *Parivāra*, with a counterpart in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pācittiya 151) [SuttaCentral]. Comprehensive parallels exist across all major Vinaya lineages—including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Lokottaravāda traditions—preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan translations [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus supports these alignments, recording cross-language matches with the Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra*, the Tibetan *Vinayasūtra* (D4117), *Bhikṣuṇīprātimokṣasūtra* (D0004), and *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon and its exegetical literature, DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse across Khandhaka chapters dealing with settlement and formal acts (such as the *Samathakkhandhaka*, *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka*, and *Kammakkhandhaka*), other Vibhaṅga rules (e.g., Pācittiya 12), and later subcommentaries including the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
